newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot gas stronger on short supply, NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot gas stronger on short supply, NYMEX.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices climbed in light volume on Wednesday as Alberta supplies fell short of expectations and the strong U.S. market provided more upward pressure, traders said.

Spot gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was pegged at C$1.47 per gigajoule, up one to two cents from Tuesday and week-ago numbers. September AECO gas was quoted at C$1.40 per GJ, down a cent from Tuesday.
"Field gas just wasn't there again and prices down south have been pushing the market up," said one Calgary-based marketer.
NYMEX and U.S. cash prices have climbed steadily since late July, with the NYMEX September contract rising to a high of US$2.59 on Monday. It retreated and closed on Wednesday at US$2.48.
At the borders, British Columbia gas at the Huntington/Sumas point was talked at US$1.17/1.20 per million British thermal units, up five to seven cents from Tuesday and about 12 cents from last week.

Gas at Dawn and Niagara was discussed at US$2.53/2.57 per mmBtu, down about 11 cents on the day in line with the drop in NYMEX gas, a trader of eastern Canadan supply said. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
